issues.description: @ts-ignore directive suppresses TypeScript type checking for the entire import, masking potential type errors
issues.suggestion: Install type definitions for 'neverchange' (@types/neverchange) or create a declaration file (neverchange.d.ts) with proper types. If types don't exist, use a more targeted @ts-expect-error with a comment explaining why.

issues.description: Module-level mutable state 'db' typed as 'any' eliminates type safety and creates potential race conditions
issues.suggestion: Define a proper type/interface for NeverChangeDB and use it: 'let db: NeverChangeDB | null = null;'. Consider using a singleton pattern or dependency injection to manage the database instance more safely.

issues.description: Condition 'if(db) db;' has no effect - it checks if db exists but doesn't return early, allowing re-initialization
issues.suggestion: Add 'return;' statement: 'if(db) return;' or 'if(db) { return; }' to prevent re-initialization of the database instance.

issues.description: Missing space after 'if' keyword - inconsistent with common formatting standards

issues.description: Migration callback parameters typed as 'any' lose type safety
issues.suggestion: Define proper types for migration callbacks or import the type from neverchange library: 'up: async (db: NeverChangeDB) => { ... }'

issues.description: Migration callback parameters typed as 'any' lose type safety (duplicate issue)
issues.suggestion: Define proper types for migration callbacks or import the type from neverchange library: 'up: async (db: NeverChangeDB) => { ... }'

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling - error is caught and logged but not propagated to caller

issues.description: Console.log statement left in production code - should use proper logging framework
issues.suggestion: Replace console.log with a proper logger or remove debug statements from production code. Consider using a logging library with log levels.

issues.description: initDb() is not idempotent - calling it multiple times could cause issues with migration re-execution
issues.suggestion: Implement proper singleton pattern: 'if (db) return db;' at the start, or use a Promise to ensure only one initialization occurs even with concurrent calls.

codeQuality.summary: This database layer has significant quality issues that need addressing. CRITICAL CONCERNS: (1) Line 7 has a broken null check that allows re-initialization, creating potential race conditions and data corruption. (2) All database functions except initDb() lack null checks on the 'db' instance, risking runtime null reference errors. (3) Type safety is completely disabled via @ts-ignore and 'any' types throughout. SECURITY: Missing input validation on all functions could allow invalid data. No protection against empty strings, negative IDs, or excessively long text. MAINTAINABILITY: Inconsistent error handling - some functions swallow errors while others propagate them. Console.log statements in production code. Module-level mutable state makes testing difficult. PERFORMANCE: SELECT * queries are inefficient. The code uses parameterized queries correctly (preventing SQL injection), but needs proper TypeScript types, comprehensive null checks, input validation, consistent error handling, and removal of debug logging before production use.

testCoverage.summary: src/db.ts has zero test coverage. This is a critical database layer file with 6 core functions handling data persistence for a todo application. All functions lack tests, including critical paths like database initialization, data validation, error handling, and security concerns (SQL injection). The absence of tests for edge cases like empty inputs, non-existent IDs, database connection failures, and concurrent operations poses significant risk. Priority should be: 1) Security tests (SQL injection in addTodo/updateTodo), 2) Database initialization and connection handling, 3) CRUD operation happy paths, 4) Edge cases for invalid inputs and non-existent records, 5) Concurrency and transaction handling. Recommend creating src/db.test.ts with at minimum 22 test cases covering the suggested scenarios above.

refactorings.summary: The db.ts file has significant refactoring opportunities despite its recent migration to neverchange. Key issues include: (1) heavy use of 'any' types eliminating TypeScript benefits, (2) global mutable state making testing difficult, (3) inconsistent error handling with some functions swallowing errors, (4) a no-op bug in initDb that should be an early return, (5) mixing of concerns with console.log statements in data layer, and (6) lack of SQL query centralization. The highest-impact improvements would be: replacing 'any' types with proper interfaces (prevents bugs), introducing a repository class pattern (eliminates global state, improves testability), and implementing a database getter pattern (ensures initialization). Medium-priority improvements include extracting SQL queries to constants (maintainability) and removing inconsistent try-catch blocks (consistent error handling). These changes would transform the code from a procedural module with weak typing into a well-typed, testable, object-oriented data access layer.

recommendations.description: Line 7 contains a no-op statement 'if(db) db;' that has no effect, allowing the database to be re-initialized multiple times. This can cause race conditions, data corruption, and migration re-execution issues. Add 'return;' after the if condition to prevent re-initialization.

No tests exist for SQL injection protection in addTodo() and updateTodo() functions. While the code uses parameterized queries (which is correct), this critical security guarantee must be verified with tests to ensure text containing SQL special characters like quotes and semicolons cannot execute malicious SQL.

Database initialization (initDb) has zero test coverage despite being critical infrastructure. Failure here breaks the entire application. Must verify schema creation succeeds, error handling works, and the function is idempotent when called multiple times. Add tests before production use.

All database operation functions (addTodo, getTodos, toggleTodo, updateTodo, deleteTodo) access the module-level 'db' variable without checking if it's null, risking runtime null reference errors if initDb() wasn't called first. Add null checks or implement a getDb() helper function that throws a clear error.

The @ts-ignore directive at line 1 and 'any' types throughout (lines 3, 13, 25) eliminate TypeScript's type safety benefits. This masks potential type errors and removes IDE autocomplete. Replace 'any' with proper types/interfaces for NeverChangeDB, define a Todo interface, and add proper return types to all functions.
